head.text: SMS Character Counter: Segments & GSM-7 vs UCS-2

attrs.content: Free SMS character counter. Paste your message to see character count, encoding (GSM-7 or Unicode), how many segments it will bill as, and what pushes it over the limit.
attrs.name: description

If the message contains any character outside GSM-7 it switches to UCS-2 (Unicode) at sixteen bits per character and the limit drops to 70 characters."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Why is my SMS counted as multiple messages?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Messages longer than one segment are split into parts, and each part carries a six-byte header. That reduces the payload to 153 characters per part in GSM-7 and 67 per part in UCS-2, so a 161-character message bills as two segments and a 307-character message as three."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Do emojis reduce the SMS character limit?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. A single emoji forces the whole message into UCS-2 encoding, cutting the single-segment limit from 160 characters to 70. Most emoji also occupy two units rather than one. Curly quotes, en and em dashes, the ellipsis character and non-breaking spaces have the same effect."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Which characters count as two in an SMS?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"In GSM-7 the extension-table characters each count as two: the caret, curly braces, square brackets, tilde, backslash, pipe and the euro sign. They do not force Unicode encoding, but they do consume two of your 160 characters each."}}]}]}
